input: SYNTHETIC, constructed from a real patch. A maintainer changes the similarity-cut script so that a flat cluster-count curve (1000, 1001, 1002 clusters at three cuts, no separation column) returns REFUSE instead of choosing the second cut. They rerun that one curve, see REFUSE with exit 2, mark the patch verified and adopt the script's output for the next cut sweep. No curve that genuinely saturates was run through the patched script, and the case-suite audit was not run on the patched copy. Rule on adopting the patched script.

The queue script is run on a batch of 1,071 counted candidates with 535 survivors and a survivor target of 600. It prints observed 535/1071 = 0.500, 95% interval [0.513, 0.514], optimistic queue 127, point 131, pessimistic 127, and LICENSED with spread 1.0x. The same script raises ZeroDivisionError on a batch of 1,072. The team proposes to plan paid-tier enumeration against the point queue of 131. Rule on the queue.

A corrected queue script replaces a midpoint-sum beta integral with a log-space continued fraction. On the three batches the documentation cites (7 of 40, 1 of 6, 9 of 250) its output is byte-identical to the old script. On a batch of 1 survivor in 30 the optimistic queue moves from 575 to 576, because the upper bound moves from 0.172174 to 0.172169; an independent library gives 0.172169 to within 5e-16. The disposition is unchanged (PROVISIONAL, 40x spread). Rule on re-deriving the queue with the corrected script.

The replay scoring script is changed so that the case listing never prints polarity and polarity is read from a separate held-out file. With one fixed verdict file, the stdout of audit and of score on the development, sealed and all sets is hashed on three copies: the original script, the changed script before the polarity column is split out, and the changed script after the split. All four hashes are identical across the three copies, and the exit codes match. Rule on scoring the next replay with the changed script.
